t: This Act shall take effect on the ninetieth day after the date of its enactment.

fable.w: This is a bare effective-date provision that only states when the Act takes effect. There is no tempting contrary reading: it mentions no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government is involved in any federal decision.
fable.s: This Act shall take effect on the ninetieth day after the date of its enactment.

qwen_block.w: This section is a standard effective date clause. It specifies when the law becomes operative but does not involve any consultation, coordination, or interaction with parties outside the federal government. There are no advisory boards, public comment periods, or requirements for outside input mentioned.
qwen_block.s: This Act shall take effect on the ninetieth day after the date of its enactment.

opus.w: This section only says when the Act takes effect. No outside party (states, tribes, the public, experts or companies) is consulted or involved in any federal decision. The 90-day delay is not a comment period or any other kind of participation, so it does not qualify.
opus.b:
1. **Tempting-but-wrong reading:** None really. A 90-day delay before the Act takes effect might look like a waiting period that could allow for public input. But the section creates no comment period, hearing, consultation or other process involving anyone outside the federal government. It only sets the effective date.
